sites.name: Edinburgh Castle
sites.summary: Iconic fortress perched magnificently on a volcanic rock above the city. The castle has been continuously used for 1100 years and is kept in excellent condition

sites.name: Holyrood Palace

sites.name: Scottish National Gallery
sites.summary: This holds much of Scotland's fine artwork from Renaissance to 20th century, with changing exhibitions.

sites.name: St Giles' Cathedral
sites.summary: It's often called a Cathedral, but the Church of Scotland brooks no such episcopal entity, and Charles I dubbing it "cathedral" in 1633 was one reason his head

sites.name: National Museum of Scotland
sites.summary: Superb museum of Scotland's heritage. You enter into the lofty Victorian Grand Gallery, where the millennium clock chimes on the hour.

sites.name: Scott Monument
sites.summary: Sir Walter Scott (1771-1832) re-invented Scotland. In the late Georgian era, he popularised tales of its medieval and Jacobean tumults, and created the clan tar

sites.name: Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh
sites.summary: Impressive gardens with a large collection. Great place to wander around on a sunny day, or to sit and have a picnic.

sites.name: HMY Britannia
sites.summary: This ship was commissioned in 1954 and was the royal transport and residence on overseas tours until 1997.

sites.name: Arthur's Seat
sites.summary: A sight in Edinburgh, Scotland, named by 2 independent sources.

sites.name: Craigmillar Castle

sites.name: Royal Observatory
sites.summary: This opened in 1896 to replace the observatory on Calton Hill in New Town (which remained active to 2009 but is now an art exhibition space).

sites.name: St Mary's Cathedral
sites.summary: The Roman Catholic Cathedral was established as a chapel in 1814 and became a cathedral in 1886 for the archdiocese of Edinburgh and St Andrews.

sites.name: Calton Hill
sites.summary: This is the stubby crag just east of Princes Street: a short stroll up it commands great views.

sites.name: Edinburgh Zoo
sites.summary: The pandas have returned to China but there's still plenty here. Penguins include gentoo, rockhopper and king, most famously Major General Sir Nils Olav III, Ba

sites.name: Edinburgh Central Mosque
sites.summary: Stately mosque and minaret completed in 1998 in a modern variant of Turkish style. You can generally look in between prayer times.
